bibliography.checked_against: the report's cover and title page (Greene_etal_2009.front0.pdf, from https://penbay.org/hapc/asmfc09/hms9_diadro_habitat_2009_0.pdf)
bibliography.note: ASMFC Habitat Management Series #9, January 2009; prepared by Karen E. Greene, Jennifer L. Zimmerman, R. Wilson Laney and Jessie C. Thomas-Blate. Matches. The alewife chapter is ch. 4, pp. 73–108. ASMFC's landing page: https://asmfc.org/resources/habitat-special-report/atlantic-coast-diadromous-fish-habitat-a-review-of-utilization-threats-recommendations-for-conservation-and-research-needs/

claims.claim: adult upper incipient lethal temperature 23.5–24 °C at 10–20 °C acclimation (via Greene et al. 2009)
claims.source_value: 23.5–24.0 °C for adults acclimated at 10, 15 and 20 °C (Otto et al. 1976); UILT defined as the temperature at which 50 % survive
claims.quote: ranged from 23.5°C to 24.0°C for adults that were acclimated at temperatures of 10°C
claims.conditions: laboratory; Otto et al. 1976 (Lake Michigan alewife, i.e. landlocked; the review warns that most tolerance data come from landlocked populations)
claims.note: Name the primary: Otto et al. 1976, via Greene et al. 2009. The same paragraph gives much higher adult UILTs from other studies: 29.8 and 32.8 °C at 16.9 and 24.5 °C acclimation (Stanley & Holzer 1971) and 31–34 °C after acclimation at 27 °C (McCauley & Binkowski 1982); the table gives only the lowest set.

claims.claim: no alewife survive below 3 °C (via Greene et al. 2009)
claims.source_value: in Otto et al. (1976) no fish survived below 3 °C regardless of acclimation temperature; lower incipient lethal range 6–8 °C for adults acclimated at 15 and 21 °C; juveniles 'cannot survive water temperatures of 3°C or below' (p. 86)
claims.quote: no fish survived below 3°C, regardless of acclimation temperature

claims.claim: juveniles need ≥ 3.6 mg/L O₂ (Jones et al. 1988, via Greene et al. 2009)
claims.source_value: minimum dissolved oxygen for juveniles 3.6 mg/L (Jones et al. 1988)
claims.quote: minimum dissolved oxygen concentration for juveniles is 3.6 mg/L
claims.note: Jones et al. (1988) give 5.0 mg/L for adults (p. 80) and for eggs and larvae (p. 83); juveniles were stressed below 2.0 mg/L (Dorfman & Westman 1970, p. 88).

claims.claim: alewife spawn mostly at night (Graham 1956, via Greene et al. 2009)
claims.source_value: may spawn throughout the day, but most spawning occurs at night (Graham 1956)
claims.quote: Alewife may spawn throughout the day, however, most spawning occurs at night

claims.claim: spawning at 0.15–3 m (row sources: Graham 1956 and Murdy et al. 1997, via Greene et al. 2009)
claims.source_value: as shallow as 15 cm (Bigelow & Schroeder 1953; Rothschild 1962) or as deep as 3 m (Edsall 1964); typically less than 1 m (Murdy et al. 1997)
claims.quote: Water depth in spawning habitat may be a mere 15 cm deep
claims.note: The range is right but its limits come from Bigelow & Schroeder 1953, Rothschild 1962 and Edsall 1964 (via Greene); Murdy et al. 1997 supplies 'typically less than 1 m', which the row could add.

claims.claim: spawning over sand, gravel, stone, plants or detritus
claims.source_value: sand, gravel or coarse stone, to submerged vegetation or organic detritus (Edsall 1964; Mansueti & Hardy 1967; Jones et al. 1978)
claims.quote: can range from sand, gravel, or coarse stone substrates, to submerged vegetation or organic detritus
claims.note: Primaries are Edsall 1964, Mansueti & Hardy 1967 and Jones et al. 1978, not Graham or Murdy.

notes: status read-part: only the alewife chapter (whole, pp. 73–108) and the front matter were fetched; nothing the paper uses lies outside them. The row's hatch-time and unfed-larva values (13 d at 7.8 °C, 2–3 d at 20–21 °C; 3.8/7.6/2.4 d) are NOT in Greene: they are from Edsall 1970's abstract, cited separately in the row. Greene relays Edsall 1970's median hatch times instead: 2.1 d at 28.9 °C, 3.9 d at 20.6 °C and 15 d at 7.2 °C (p. 82), hatching 2–15 days depending on temperature (Fay et al. 1983) and most often in 3–5 days (Edsall 1970); spawning ceases at 27.8 °C (Edsall 1970, p. 79). Other usable values: yolk absorbed and first feeding 2–5 d after hatch (p. 82); juvenile UILT slightly under 26.5, 30.3 and 32.1 °C at 10, 20 and 25 °C acclimation (Otto et al. 1976, p. 87).
